title: The same JTRSY credit exposure is reached through two structurally different conduits with independent limits ten times apart
content:
JTRSY appears twice in this chunk. On Ethereum Mainnet (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.1) it is a "Tokenized Treasury JTRSY" Instance: Target Protocol Centrifuge, Asset Supplied **USDS**, with seven addresses including a Centrifuge ERC-7540 Vault, a Rate Provider, a Pocket Contract, a Token Redeemer, an Owner Timelock and a Basin Contract — plus Interim Deployment status, 100% CRR, and a 5,000,000 USDS inflow limit.

On Avalanche (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.2.1.1) it is a "Centrifuge JTRSY" Instance: Target Protocol Centrifuge, Asset Supplied **USDC**, with two addresses — token and underlying asset — no Basin, no Pocket, no Redeemer, no timelock, no interim status, and an inflow `maxAmount` of **50,000,000 USDC** (.2.1.1.2.4.1).

Same issuer, same fund, same underlying credit risk; a tenfold difference in authorized inflow and an entirely different control apparatus. The Ethereum route is treated as an unproven deployment requiring full capital backing and a five-contract scaffold; the Avalanche route is treated as a routine conduit at ten times the size.

The defensible reading is that the *deployment* is what is being tested on Ethereum — the Basin architecture, the Pocket/Redeemer split, the timelock — not JTRSY itself, and that the Avalanche Instance predates it. But that reading has a consequence the documents do not address: nothing aggregates the two. Credit exposure to one Centrifuge fund is bounded twice, per-network, with no ceiling spanning them, so the conservatism of the interim 5,000,000 cap is undermined by a 50,000,000 path to the same risk on another chain.

This is the cross-network form of the aggregation gap: Grove's Instance boundary is *(venue, network, operation)*, while credit risk is a property of the issuer, and the schema provides no slot where issuer-level exposure is summed.
description: Ethereum JTRSY routes USDS through an ERC-7540 vault, Pocket, Redeemer and Basin with a 5m interim cap; Avalanche JTRSY routes USDC through a bare token address with a 50m inflow limit.
